title: Streaming fragment orchestration, schema handoff, and fallback acceptance
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Purpose: Define acceptance criteria and rollout plan for a streaming-first structured-output contract that guarantees parseable partial emissions, deterministic tool/function-call handoff, and graceful fallback modes. Scope: runtime framing (fragment envelopes), SDK parser behavior, telemetry/QA, and rollout gating. Out of scope for this ticket: transactional multi-call rollback semantics (deferred to PM-110045) and language-specific SDK idiomatic wrappers; those will be follow-ups. Background: customers building multi-step workflows require that streamed JSON (or typed fragments) can be validated and handed to tool runners without requiring the full-response to be present. Past incidents revealed two failure modes: (1) partial emission that cannot be reassembled unambiguously, (2) opaque tool-invocation frames that the tool proxy cannot safely retry. This PRD consolidates acceptance into concrete tests and implementation checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Frame format: Every streamed fragment emitted by the model runtime must be wrapped in a 'frame' envelope with the following flat attributes: frame_id, sequence_index (int), frame_type (one of: schema, data, tool_call, checkpoint, error), schema_id (optional), and optional resume_token. The SDK and runtime must be able to detect and ignore unknown envelope fields without failing parsing.

Progressive schema handshake: The first non-empty schema frame in a stream must include a stable schema_id and a version string. Consumers (SDK/runtime) must validate that subsequent data frames either reference that schema_id or include an explicit schema frame before switching. A schema switch mid-stream without a referenced schema frame is considered a schema violation.

Partial-parseability: Any prefix of the stream that ends at a checkpoint frame must be parseable into a well-formed partial object (no dangling commas, unclosed arrays/objects) by the SDK's incremental parser. The SDK must expose a 'partial_object' with provenance metadata (frames included, sequence range, resume_token).

Tool/function call semantics: Tool-call frames must contain a unique call_id (UUID), target_tool (string), payload (stringified JSON), and idempotency_token. The tool proxy must accept repeated call attempts deduplicated by call_id or idempotency_token. Calls declared 'fire_and_forget' are allowed but must be explicitly marked.

Idempotency & replay: If a stream disconnects, a client using the resume_token must be able to replay from the last checkpoint without triggering duplicate side effects when a call_id or idempotency_token is present. The runtime must provide deterministic checkpoint tokens tied to sequence_index and last-committed-call_id.

Error taxonomy and recovery behaviors: Define three error classes emitted as error frames: recoverable_retryable (transient parser or network), failover_fallback (model output invalid but another fallback model or simplified payload can be emitted), and final_error (no retry). Acceptance requires telemetry that classifies error frames and that fallbacks are executed according to route policy (e.g., fallback_model -> reduced_schema_mode -> final_error).

Backpressure and soft-stop: If downstream tooling signals backpressure, runtime must emit a checkpoint frame and either pause streaming or switch to compact/resume_mode. SDK must surface a 'backpressure' hint and provide a 'resume' API that accepts a resume_token.

Observability: For every stream that contains tool_call frames, the runtime must emit events to tracing with: stream_id, client_id, call_id list, time_to_first_tool_frame, number_of_checkpoints, and final_stream_outcome. Acceptance requires a Grafana dashboard and an alert on tool_call failure_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m for beta customers.

Compatibility: New frame envelopes must be backward compatible. If an older SDK receives a stream with unknown frame_type values it must ignore unknown frames and surface raw unparsed text in a 'legacy_raw' property. Acceptance demands a compatibility test suite covering at least two older SDK versions used in the field.

E2E tests: There must be deterministic e2e tests that validate: resume in middle of tool_call, mid-stream schema switch with explicit schema frame, and simulated partial truncation leading to graceful degrade to fallback_model. Tests must run in CI and be included in the regression suite.

Security: Tool_call frames that include secrets must be redacted in observability output and comply with KMS policies. Acceptance requires a security review checklist sign-off and a minimal linting pass that flags any frames including keys or raw tokens.

Docs & SDKs: Acceptance requires updated protocol docs, a migration guide for existing streaming users, and sample integrations in Node and Python SDKs demonstrating resume_token usage and parsing partial objects.
decisions: Use a flat JSON envelope for frames (not binary length-prefix) to simplify proxy inspection and playback across our gateway.
Adopt idempotency driven by call_id + optional idempotency_token. call_id is primary dedupe key.
Checkpoint granularity: emit checkpoint every N frames or when a tool_call completes; configurable per-route (default N=10).
Fallback policy will be runtime-configurable with prioritized actions: fallback_model -> reduced_schema_mode -> emit_error_frame -> final_failure.
tradeoffs: Flat JSON envelopes increase bandwidth compared to compact binary framing but simplify debugging and compatibility with existing proxies.
Stricter checkpointing increases cost and slightly higher latency on small streams; tradeoff accepted for strong resume guarantees for high-impact customers.
Placing dedupe responsibility on call_id requires clients to generate stable UUIDs; if clients do not, dedupe may be weaker—mitigated by offering SDK helpers.
